characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; samples etched with 6 % Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1 showed a light polygonal ferrite-containing matrix at 1050 °C but was αp-free at 1150 °C (labelled 'αp - free'); no αp reported for S1 at 1150 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LOM at 1050 °C benchmark and at the selected TA = 1150 °C for S1 (100 µm scale bars)
characterization_methods.purpose: Verify polygonal ferrite (αp) retention/elimination after austenitization

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; gold sputter coating on etched samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1 at 300 °C shows fine parallel needle/lath bainite with arrows pointing to (Fe,M)xCy.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM of S1 austempered at 300 °C (500 nm scale bar) and at 350 °C (1 µm scale bar)
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal nano-bainitic morphology and precipitates; measure bainitic lamella thickness (100 measurements from 10 images)

characterization_methods.key_findings: EDX confirmed (Fe,M)xCy cementite-like carbides modified by Si and Mo; Si interpreted as entrapped by rapid cooling.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EDX chemical analysis of precipitates (Spec.1–3 for S1&S2)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitate composition (Fe,M)xCy; detect Si and Mo in the particles

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu X-ray tube, 40 kV/40 mA, PIXcel 1D detector (TU Clausthal, Institute of Non-Metallic Materials)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 2(a) shows the S1 XRD pattern used to determine Vγ; S1 at TB 300 °C gives Vγ = 27 %, εγ = 0.50 %, εα = 0.45 % (Table 3); (1 − Vc) = 0.78 from MatCalc.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cu Kα radiation; integrated intensities of (111)γ, (200)γ, (220)γ, (311)γ peaks; ASTM E975-13
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained-austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and micro-strains (εγ, εα)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured TA of S1 = 1062 °C; Ms = 277 °C; Bt = 4000 s at TB 300 °C with 80 s incubation; Bt = 1600 s at TB 350 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cylindrical specimens (ø5x10 mm^3); heating 10 K s⁻¹, cooling 100 K s⁻¹; TA detected with 1 K s⁻¹ above 1100 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine TA, Ms and bainitic transformation finish time (Bt) from RLC-time curves

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MatCalc (Version 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1 ferrite-free TA = 991 °C (MatCalc), Tcd = 1103 °C; (1 − Vc) = 0.78; TTP diagram for S1 (approx. representative of S2) shows (Fe,M)xCy precipitating between ~700 °C and 1150 °C during cooling.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Standard step calculation; fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC system; cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹
characterization_methods.purpose: Assist TA/Ms analysis; assess carbide-dissolution temperature (Tcd) and precipitation kinetics for S1
characterization_methods.technique: MatCalc thermodynamic/kinetic simulation (equilibrium phase fractions and TTP)

analytical_models.equation_role: Identify the ferrite-free austenitizing temperature and complete-dissolution temperature of (Fe,M)xCy carbides from the equilibrium phase-fraction diagram
analytical_models.model_name: Ferrite-free TA and carbide-dissolution temperature (Tcd) determination
analytical_models.model_note: Grey boxes in Fig. 4(a) print TA = 991 °C and Tcd = 1103 °C with dashed arrows.

analytical_models.equation_role: Correct Vγ for the carbide fraction: Vγ = (1 − Vc)[(Iγ/Rγ)/((Iα/Rα)+(Iγ/Rγ))]
analytical_models.model_note: Fig. 2(b) MatCalc equilibrium phase fractions of S1 with the arrow labelled (1 − Vc) = 0.78; Eq. (1) in Section 2.3.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Standard step calculation method; heterogeneous nucleation theory considering only dislocation and grain-boundary sites and ortho-equilibrium transformation; volumetric misfit considered; κ-carbides treated as fixed phase fractions; simulated for the heat treatment defined for bainitic transformation (TA 1150 °C, cooling 100 K s⁻¹)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic database covering fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC; (Fe,M)xCy and Ti–Mo–C carbide systems
computational_details.simulation_method: Equilibrium phase-fraction (step) calculations and precipitation-kinetics modelling
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc (Version 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: MatCalc simulations supported the experimental findings: S1 ferrite-free TA (MatCalc) = 991 °C vs TA (measured) = 1062 °C and TA (applied) = 1150 °C; predicted complete dissolution of (Fe,M)xCy carbides around 1103–1107 °C for S1–S2; TTP indicated (Fe,M)xCy formation above the austempering temperature, consistent with SEM/EDX observation of carbides formed during prior processing.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: precipitate located at γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Rounded (Fe,M)xCy carbides formed near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; accelerated nucleation and spherical nature of these cementite-like precipitates showed no micro-void formation, hence negligible effect on mechanical properties.

interfaces.interface_notes: Retained austenite largely blocky between bainite sheaves at this condition; (Fe,M)xCy carbides detected near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During austempering at 300 °C, austenite transforms to nano-bainitic ferrite with 27 % retained austenite remaining; (Fe,M)xCy carbides are interpreted as primarily formed during prior processing/cooling rather than during the austempering hold.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: strength–ductility trade-off tuned by TB via plate thickness and retained-austenite stability

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace.
Homogenization promotes uniform composition and microstructure throughout the steel blocks.
Homogenized steel is subjected to step-by-step hot rolling, reducing its thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.

processing_steps.method: water jet cutting (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples precisely fabricated to allow accurate geometries and minimize thermal distortion; cylindrical specimens (ø5x10 mm^3) were used for heat treatments in the DIL 805A dilatometer.

Fig. 1(a) thermal cycle: S1, S2, S5: 1150 °C (15 min). Fixed austenitization temperature of 1150 °C applied for S1, S2, S4, S5; selected above the measured/calculated TA so that the microstructure is αp-free and carbides dissolve.

processing_steps.method: continuous cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹, sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations and ensure fine bainitic transformation.
TB = 300 °C; transformation duration measured as 4000 s for S1 (Bt, near-full bainitic transformation). Incubation time 80 s. Selected just above the measured Ms (277 °C).

processing_steps.method: final cooling after isothermal bainitic hold
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fig. 1(a) thermal cycle ends with final cooling after the isothermal bainitic hold.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests carried out on a Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell); all specimens heat-treated in the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the Fig. 1(a) cycle. Specimens tested at TA 1150 °C / TB 300 °C.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
mechanically grinded and polished samples for XRD (Malvern Panalytical Empyrean, Cu Kα, 40 kV/40 mA); SEM lamella thickness measured from 10 SEM images, 10 measurements each (100 per condition)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Dilatometric RLC-time analysis to define Bt; Ms determined by tangent-intersection on cooling at 100 K/s
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimens (ø5x10 mm^3) in DIL 805A dilatometer

phases_present.morphology: fine parallel needle/lath bainite (nano-bainitic), type 1 and type 2 nB sheaves
blocky γr regions between bainite sheaves

precipitates.distribution: located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; only detectable by localized brightness under SEM

structures.overall_structure: αp-free nano-bainitic (nB) microstructure after austenitizing S1 at 1150 °C and austempering at 300 °C; no polygonal ferrite (αp) detected (Table 3 marks αp as '-'), LOM at 1150 °C labelled 'αp - free'.

unmapped_findings: PSE (product of strength and elongation) for S1 at TA 1150 °C / TB 300 °C = 10,880 MPa·% (corresponding to UTS ~1600 MPa and El 6.8 %); at TB 350 °C the PSE increased to ~12,000 MPa·% (UTS ~1380 MPa, El 8.7 %). (b0063)

S1 austempered at 300 °C: transformation duration (bainite finish time, Bt) = 4000 s and incubation time = 80 s; at 350 °C, Bt = 1600 s and incubation time = 100 s. S1 consistently showed shorter incubation periods than S2 under both austempering conditions. (b0042)

True lamellar thickness Lt(t) of S1 at TA 1150 °C / TB 300 °C = 35 nm with SD 11 nm; at TB 350 °C Lt(t) = 55 nm with SD 23 nm. Lt(t) was calculated from the mean linear intercept with the stereological correction Lt(t) = 2Lt/π (100 measurements from 10 SEM images per condition). (b0023, b0074)
Retained austenite Vγ of S1 at TB 300 °C = 27 %; at TB 350 °C = 34 %, i.e. higher austempering temperature gives a more pronounced incomplete-reaction (higher Vγ) in S1. (b0070, b0074)
At the 1050 °C benchmark S1 displayed a dual-phase structure with αp; at the applied TA of 1150 °C S1 was αp-free (Table 3 αp = '-'). (b0033, b0074)

Measured austenitizing temperature of S1 = 1062 °C (dilatometry derivative criterion), MatCalc ferrite-free TA = 991 °C, carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd = 1103 °C, and the applied TA = 1150 °C; the measured Ms = 277 °C. (b0033, b0035, figure_002, figure_004)

Micro-strain values for S1 at TB 300 °C: εγ = 0.50 % (austenite) and εα = 0.45 % (bainitic ferrite); no significant ε difference between the phases was observed at this condition, whereas at TB 350 °C εα was notably higher (0.30–0.45 %). (b0075, b0074)

MatCalc TTP diagram for S1 (also approximately representative of S2): header TA 1150 °C, cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹; (Fe,M)xCy precipitation curves (5 %, 50 %, 95 %) with a C-shaped nose near 900–1000 °C at ~10⁻³–10⁻² s; dashed TB lines at 350 °C (Bt: 2300 s) and 300 °C (Bt: 3600 s). (figure_008, b0079)
S1 and S2 exhibit only minor differences in mechanical performance, indicating that a 0.1 wt.% variation in carbon content has a negligible effect on the overall mechanical response. (b0063)

The (Fe,M)xCy precipitates observed in S1 had a rounded morphology inconsistent with spinodal decomposition (nucleation-driven formation), were located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries, and are interpreted as formed primarily during prior processing/cooling rather than during austempering; their stabilization is attributed to rapid cooling and residual Mo and Si in the particles. (b0084, b0112, b0082)
